validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed as a distinct, completed FERC-tracked expansion project, not a GEM-only entity. EIA's own 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' pipeline-projects table (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, downloaded and parsed directly with openpyxl - the wiki's cited 'Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects' link is only the navigation page, so I went to the actual workbook it points to) carries a row named exactly 'Alabama Compressor Station Upgrade', Pipeline Operator Name 'AlaTenn Pipeline', Project Type 'Expansion', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2020-10-08, Docket Number CP19-476, Authority FERC, Cost (millions) 5.4, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 38.5, notes 'Increase compression on AlaTenn pipeline and increase deliveries to growing demand in Alabama; flow through compressor will increase from 59 MMcf/d to 97 MMcf/d.' Independently, the Federal Register notice of the underlying FERC filing (govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-06-18/pdf/2019-12814.pdf, 84 FR 28297, Docket CP19-476-000) confirms American Midstream (AlaTenn), LLC filed June 3, 2019 to abandon 4 old compressor units (1,455 hp) and install 2 new units (3,550 hp) at its Decatur Compression Station, Limestone County, Alabama, 'to provide additional firm transportation service to the City of Huntsville, Alabama, d/b/a Huntsville Utilities and improve system reliability,' estimated cost $5,415,200 (url_verifier's substring check false-negatived on the exact dollar string and en-dash-encoded docket number - a known PDF-extraction artifact per the tool's own docs; I confirmed both by hand with pdftotext -layout). A third, wholly independent origin - the current operator's own live site, blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission - still lists 'AlaTenn: FERC-Regulated Interstate, 325 miles, 2-20 inch, 550-977# MAOP, 292 MDth/d capacity' among Black Bear's active systems today, confirming Status=operating is still correct as of 2026, not stale. PipelineType=transmission is correct: AlaTenn is explicitly a FERC-regulated interstate natural-gas TRANSMISSION system (Black Bear's own site header; the FR notice describes 'additional firm transportation service'), not a gathering/process line. CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE: GEM correctly tracks this expansion as its own segment row separate from the AlaTenn mainline. The fresh GGIT snapshot (2026-09-04) confirms P0185 = 'AlaTenn Gas Pipeline' with no SegmentName, LengthKnown=475 km/295 mi, Capacity=200 MMcf/d, StartYear1=2002 - the base trunk described in the wiki's 'Project Details' section (from Selmer, TN to Huntsville, AL) - while P2500 carries the wiki's separate 'Expansion Projects > Alabama Compressor Station Upgrade' figures (LengthKnown=0, Capacity=39, StartYear1=2020, Cost ~$5M), matching a compression-only capacity add with no new pipe. This is the correct GEM convention (LengthKnown=0/Diameter=blank for an expansion adding no new physical pipe) and not a duplicate/relabel of P0185 or of any other roster row - no other roster pipeline's geography or figures overlap with this Alabama compressor project. Capacity is essentially confirmed but not exact: GEM's 39.00 MMcf/d is a ~1.3% rounding of the EIA/FERC-derived 38.5 MMcf/d (59->97 MMcf/d differential); immaterial, not staged as a concern, but the more precise EIA figure is offered in the Capacity fill for Baird's consideration. Opened all 10 of this row's harvested wiki citations: 2 (Wikipedia mirror, Bloomberg private-company snapshot) are stale/paywalled and not chased further (they only ever supported historical ownership predating Black Bear, already superseded); the businesswire.com acquisition release 403s to a scripted UA (confirmed via Wayback, see the Owner fill) and is a system-level (not AlaTenn-specific) press release, so it is used only as owner-chain context, not a segment ref; the FERC tariff-index PDF and the generic eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php page are both navigation/index surfaces, not citable for any one value; the remaining 6 (blackbearllc.com x2, PGJ 2017 - confirmed dead, 404, no Wayback capture - EnergyTech 2023, eia.gov data.php) were opened and are folded into this finding and the fills below. Also opened 6 sources found via open-web search beyond the wiki pool: the EIA historical-projects xlsx itself, the Federal Register/govinfo PDF, a PHMSA public-awareness brochure (pipelinesafetyinfo.com), a PHMSA PRIMIS enforcement notice (Nov 2025), and 2 trade-press pieces (pgjonline.com, worldpipelines.com/businesswire via search) on the 2025 Enstor-Black Bear acquisition.
